from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Key Invariant: Genus (The 'Hole' Count)", 
                          ["Genus is the hole count.", 
                           "It is a topological invariant.", 
                           "Different genus means distinct topology.", 
                           "Soccer ball has zero holes.", 
                           "Donut has one hole."])
        
        # Objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_opacity(0.6)
        donut = Torus(major_radius=0.5, minor_radius=0.2, color=GREEN).set_opacity(0.6)
        double_torus = VGroup(
            Torus(major_radius=0.3, minor_radius=0.15, color="#FF4500"),
            Torus(major_radius=0.3, minor_radius=0.15, color="#FF4500")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        label0 = Text("Genus 0", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("Genus 1", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        label2 = Text("Genus 2", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Genus is the hole count. ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label0, 'A2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(label0))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: It is a topological invariant. ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(donut, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(donut), Write(label1))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: Different genus means distinct topology. ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(double_torus, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(double_torus), Write(label2))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4: Soccer ball has zero holes. ===

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Euler Characteristic", [
            "Euler characteristic is constant.",
            "Formula: Vertices minus edges plus faces.",
            "Always equals two for convex polyhedra."
        ])
        
        # Define colors for V, E, F
        c_v = "#FF6B6B" # Red
        c_e = "#4ECDC4" # Teal
        c_f = "#FFE66D" # Yellow
        
        formula = MathTex(r"V - E + F = 2", font_size=42)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("V", c_v)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("E", c_e)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("F", c_f)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87CEEB")) # Sky Blue
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("V: Vertices", font_size=20, color=c_v),
            Text("E: Edges", font_size=20, color=c_e),
            Text("F: Faces", font_size=20, color=c_f)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(labels, "D3")
        self.play(Write(labels))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, "E5")
        self.play(Create(cube))
        
        result = Text("= 2", font_size=36, color="#FFD700")
        result.next_to(formula, RIGHT)
        self.play(Write(result))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Topology", ["Topology categorizes complex shapes.", "Used in DNA and robotics.", "Persistence defines the object."])
        
        # Define objects
        # 1. Map (represented by a cluster of points and lines)
        city_points = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[pos], radius=0.08, color=WHITE) for pos in ["A2", "A5", "C2", "C5", "E3"]])
        city_lines = VGroup(
            Line(city_points[0].get_center(), city_points[1].get_center(), color=GRAY),
            Line(city_points[0].get_center(), city_points[2].get_center(), color=GRAY),
            Line(city_points[1].get_center(), city_points[3].get_center(), color=GRAY),
            Line(city_points[2].get_center(), city_points[4].get_center(), color=GRAY),
            Line(city_points[3].get_center(), city_points[4].get_center(), color=GRAY)
        )
        map_network = VGroup(city_points, city_lines)
        
        # 2. Topological Graph
        graph_network = map_network.copy().set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(map_network))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(map_network, graph_network))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        data_pulse = Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW).move_to(city_points[0].get_center())
        self.play(Create(data_pulse))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(data_pulse, city_lines[0]), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(data_pulse))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Introduction to Topology: The Geometry of Rubber Sheets
outline.target_audience: University students (non-math majors or early undergraduates)

sections.title: The Hook: Geometry vs. Topology
sections.content: Define topology as 'rubber-sheet geometry.' Explain that unlike standard geometry (which cares about distances and angles), topology ignores stretching and bending, focusing only on properties that remain invariant under continuous deformation.
sections.example: Visualize a coffee mug and a donut made of play-dough. Show an animation where the mug is smoothly molded into the shape of a donut without tearing or gluing.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Homeomorphism
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Homeomorphism.' Two objects are topologically equivalent if one can be transformed into the other via a continuous deformation (bijective mapping). Crucially, we cannot tear, cut, or glue the shape.
sections.example: Display an animation of a square being stretched into a circle. Because we can map every point on the square to the circle without cutting, they are homeomorphic.

sections.title: The Key Invariant: Genus (The 'Hole' Count)
sections.content: Explain that the number of holes is a fundamental topological invariant. This integer is called the 'genus.' Objects with different numbers of holes are topologically distinct.
sections.example: Compare a soccer ball (Genus 0, no holes), a donut (Genus 1, one hole), and a pair of glasses (Genus 2, two holes/loops). Explain why a soccer ball can never be turned into a donut without puncturing it.

sections.title: The Famous Application: The Euler Characteristic
sections.content: Briefly introduce the formula V - E + F = 2 (Vertices - Edges + Faces). Explain how this formula stays constant for any convex polyhedron regardless of its specific shape, proving it is a topological property.
sections.example: Show a cube and a tetrahedron. Count their vertices, edges, and faces to demonstrate that they both result in 2, illustrating that they share the same underlying 'topological DNA'.

sections.title: Real-World Conclusion: Why Topology Matters
sections.content: Summarize how topology is used in modern science, from DNA supercoiling in biology to networking and data analysis. Final thought: Topology allows us to categorize complex shapes by their simplest, most persistent traits.
sections.example: Mention how a biologist identifies 'knots' in DNA strands, or how a roboticist plans a path for a robot arm by mapping the 'topological space' of its joints.
